Strikingly, CA-V inhibition also mitigates caspase activation and endothelial cell activation in the brains of 3xTg AD mice, resulting in preserved memory function. Our results demonstrate that selective CA-V inhibition is an effective and promising strategy against AD-mediated cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment.

articles_hidden.title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse Malat1 long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
articles_hidden.authors: Wen Xiao, Tanja Hann, Zion Perry, Vijaya Pandey, Jeffrey Cheng, James Wohlschlegel, Anna Marie Pyle, Douglas L. Black
articles_hidden.abstract: In most cells, Malat1 long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons, Malat1 is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame. In vivo chemical probing and structural modeling defined a three-stem-loop RNA secondary structure that encompasses the active IRES segment and coincides with a mouse B1 SINE (short interspersed element) repetitive element. In affinity purification experiments, a minimal IRES/B1 RNA selectively bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors, and the known IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1. Depletion of Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 inhibited IRES-dependent translation of the reporter and expression of the endogenous M1 peptide. Our study identifies an unexpected functional unit hidden within a widely studied long noncoding RNA.

articles_hidden.title: Humans experienced abrupt environmental changes at White Sands during the Last Glacial Maximum
articles_hidden.authors: Kathleen B. Springer, Jeffrey S. Pigati, Jessica E. Tierney, Jeffrey S. Honke, Gonzalo Jiménez-Moreno, David Bustos, Thomas M. Urban, Daniel Odess, Edward A. Jolie, Alison J. Smith, Abigail J. Hunt, Patrick J. Martinez, Vincent L. Santucci, Sally C. Reynolds, Matthew R. Bennett
articles_hidden.abstract: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park have unearthed 20 stratigraphic horizons containing in situ human footprints, megafaunal trackways, and linear features created by travois. Advances in radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, combined with ages of aquatic seeds, refines the chronology of the footprint-bearing sequence to between 23.5 and 21.7 thousand years ago (ka). Biomarker, pollen, and stratigraphic evidence indicate a complete overturning of the environment from a perennial lake to a playa and capture a large aridification episode coincident with Dansgaard-Oeschger event 2 at 23.2 ka, which shrank pluvial Lake Otero and allowed people to traverse the former shoreline area for nearly two millennia. This well-dated and highly resolved paleoclimate record provides compelling evidence that humans in North America experienced marked environmental changes during the Last Glacial Maximum.

articles_hidden.title: Influenza A virus infection induces immune dysregulation in the placenta and fetus without vertical transmission in nonhuman primates
articles_hidden.authors: Orlando Cervantes, Sidney Sun, Hazel Huang, Briana Del Rosario, Hong Zhao, Amanda Li, Andrew Vo, Gygeria Manuel, Roslyn Van Abel, Jeff Munson, John Cornelius, Raj P. Kapur, Miranda Li, Edmunda Li, Hanning Li, Alexandra Christodoulou, Melissa Berg, Britni Curtis, Elizabeth Miller, Shannon Ruff, Brenna Menz, Solomon Wangari, Audrey Germond, Audrey Baldessari, Chris English, W. McIntyre Durning, Thomas B. Lewis, Megan N. Fredericks, Mara Maughan, Austyn Orvis, Michelle Coleman, Lakshmi Rajagopal, Deborah H. Fuller, Kristina M. Adams Waldorf
articles_hidden.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) infection during pregnancy is associated with stillbirth and preterm birth. We hypothesized that maternal IAV infection disrupts placental and fetal immune networks in ways that correlate with disease severity. Pregnant pigtail macaques were inoculated with IAV [A/California/07/2009 (H1N1)] and underwent delivery and fetal necropsy 5 days postinfection ( N  = 11), with comparison to uninfected controls ( N  = 16). Stillbirth occurred in 18% of infected pregnancies and in no controls. Although vertical transmission was not observed, low levels of viral RNA were detected in two placentas. Maternal infection was associated with induction of a type I interferon response in the placenta and altered innate and adaptive immune cell populations in the fetus. Maternal disease metrics (e.g., lung viral load and interferon-α) were rarely associated with placental immune perturbations but frequently linked to fetal immune cell populations (CD4 + and CD8 + T cells and monocyte subsets). Collectively, these data indicate that maternal IAV disease severity is associated with dysregulated fetal immunity.

articles_hidden.title: Bisulfate-mediated selective methane oxidation under mild aqueous conditions
articles_hidden.authors: Shike Lu, Shao-Chun Wen, Wenxuan Liu, Haonan Li, Mu-Jeng Cheng, Bingjun Xu, Qi Lu
articles_hidden.abstract: The selective oxidation of methane under mild conditions remains a formidable challenge because of the inert C─H bond and the ease of over-oxidation. Here we report a facile strategy that enables methane conversion at room temperature and ambient pressure using molecular O 2 and commercially available Cu powder in dilute aqueous H 2 SO 4 . The reaction is capable of proceeding with only trace CO 2 formation, producing methyl bisulfate and methanol as the primary partial oxidation products. In situ Raman spectroscopy indicates that an in situ O 2 -derived Cu 2 O surface is the reaction-relevant phase associated with C─H bond activation. The observed selectivity arises from bisulfate adsorption on this Cu 2 O surface, which suppresses methanol over-oxidation, together with the interception of surface-generated methyl intermediates to form oxidation-resistant methyl bisulfate. This Cu/O 2 -H 2 SO 4 system demonstrates that methane can be selectively oxidized under mild aqueous conditions and provides mechanistic insight into Cu/O 2 -mediated oxidation, suggesting a bisulfate-assisted approach to suppressing over-oxidation that may be applicable to other substrates.

articles_hidden.title: Record-setting heavy precipitation occurrence in 2024
articles_hidden.authors: Chad W. Thackeray, Jesse Norris, Alex Hall, Mark D. Zelinka, Stephen Po-Chedley
articles_hidden.abstract: Precipitation extremes have increased globally in recent decades, consistent with a warming climate. We find that 2024 experienced a record-high frequency of heavy (≥99th percentile; F P≥99 ) precipitation events globally based on MSWEP (Multi-Source Weighted-Ensemble Precipitation) observations from 1979 to 2025. This extends a long-term trend of ∼0.03%/decade in F P≥99 , with similar but more uncertain increases for the 99.9th percentile. Unlike prior high F P≥99 years, 2024’s record was more globally distributed and emerged from a distinct seasonal evolution. El Niño and rare concurrent multi-basin tropical ocean warmth drove elevated extremes early in the year, before lagged global tropospheric responses and long-term warming sustained and amplified extremes through boreal summer. Climate models indicate that years with 2024-level F P≥99 typically require either stronger El Niño forcing or concurrent multi-basin sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies. Diagnostic projections within constrained ensemble members suggest that ∼40% of the 2024 anomaly aligns with global mean temperatures and ∼20% with El Niño variability, with some of the remainder linked to basin-scale SST structure.

articles_hidden.title: Hydration channel engineering in Tröger’s base-POP membranes for mono/multivalent cation and anion discrimination
articles_hidden.authors: Haopan Sun, Ning Gan, Baolong Wu, Chenglin Liu, Yan Jin, Yuzhu Sun, Jianguo Yu, Zhaoliang Cui, Yuqing Lin, Hideto Matsuyama, Young Moo Lee
articles_hidden.abstract: Sustainable recovery of critical resources from complex aqueous streams is constrained by membranes that fail to combine rapid ion transport with precise mono/multivalent discrimination. Here, we report Tröger’s base-derived porous organic polymer (POP) membranes with rigid, covalently crosslinked microporous frameworks that stabilize angstrom-scale transport channels while suppressing hydration-induced swelling. These membranes render rapid monovalent-ion transport with near-complete exclusion of multivalent cations and anions, including Mg 2+ , Al 3+ , SO 4 2− , and PO 4 3− . Experiments and simulations show that steric confinement, dehydration penalties, and electrostatic interactions cooperatively raise migration barriers for multivalent ions in confined channels. The membranes achieve comprehensive mono/multivalent discrimination across both cationic and anionic systems. In multistage electrodialysis, they enable stage-amplified lithium enrichment from high-Mg brines with stable long-term operation and downstream recovery of crystalline Li 2 CO 3 . They also facilitate high-purity NaCl enrichment from simulated seawater. Overall, this platform offers a durable and energy-efficient route to selective resource recovery from complex aqueous streams.

articles_hidden.title: Chromatin interaction landscape of epimorphic regeneration in teleost fish
articles_hidden.authors: Xiaohui Jia, Xianglei Zhang, Weifeng Lin, Tengfei Ren, Shiqi Liu, Yufei Lou, Wei Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Reorganization of chromatin architecture—including chromatin loops, topologically associating domains (TADs), and A/B compartments—has been increasingly linked to development and cell differentiation. However, how chromatin architecture reorganizes during the shift from homeostasis to regeneration remains poorly characterized. Here, we used zebrafish fin regeneration as a model to systematically investigate, via micro-C, the chromatin architecture associated with blastema formation. Our analyses unveiled that the alteration of chromatin looping upon amputation was dominant compared with that of TADs and compartments. Genes directly linked to injury-altered loop interactions, including essential regeneration regulators, were mainly related to morphogenesis and cell division. A side-by-side comparison between zebrafish and African killifish uncovered conserved and species-specific chromatin reorganization following injury. Notably, perturbing injury-altered loop interactions at the il11a locus suppressed its expression and impaired fin regeneration efficiency. Further, CTCF/CTCFL and Atf7 binding motifs were the top shared motifs enriched in regeneration-altered loop anchors. Our study uncovers the landscape of chromatin interactions during fin regeneration.

articles_hidden.title: Ice nucleation by kaolinite: Morphology shapes the size dependence of ice nucleation active sites on dust particles
articles_hidden.authors: Yuhang Song, Claudia Marcolli, Jie Chen, Ulrike Lohmann
articles_hidden.abstract: Mineral dusts are the most important type of ice-nucleating particles and play a key role in cloud formation and climate. Their activity is commonly assumed to scale with particle surface area, yet whether this assumption holds across particle sizes remains unverified. Here, we quantify size-dependent ice nucleation activity using compositionally pure, size-segregated kaolinite (KGa-1b). Ice nucleation active site (INAS) densities were determined for size classes from submicron to 48 μm, revealing two distinct ice-nucleation regimes. At low temperatures (∼240 K), INAS density per surface area is independent of particle size. In contrast, at warm temperatures (∼260 K), particles of 6 to 12 μm exhibit the highest INAS densities, up to two orders of magnitude greater than smaller particles and nonsize-selected bulk samples. Linking these results to particle morphology indicates that well-aligned, multilayered platelet edges provide the continuous hydroxylated surfaces required for efficient ice nucleation. Our findings demonstrate that morphology can modulate particle size–dependent ice nucleation, highlighting limitations of simple surface area–based parameterizations.

articles_hidden.title: Dishevelled-mediated clustering stabilizes Frizzled6 and Vangl2 to establish planar cell polarity in the mammalian skin
articles_hidden.authors: Parijat Sil, Brandon Trejo, Katherine A. Little, Danelle Devenport
articles_hidden.abstract: Planar cell polarity (PCP) in epithelia is characterized by the polarized distribution of two opposing, membrane-associated PCP complexes across cell junctions. Transmembrane components of the PCP complex bridge cell junctions and organize into punctate, intercellular assemblies that exhibit a high degree of stability. Here, we define the contributions of the cytoplasmic PCP protein, Dishevelled (Dvl), in the submicrometer scale organization and stability of PCP complexes. Using endogenously tagged fluorescent PCP reporters in the embryonic mouse epidermis, we quantify PCP protein mobility and clustering during polarization. We find that as transmembrane proteins immobilize into puncta, Dvl2/3 coaccumulates with its transmembrane partner Frizzled 6 in a polarized manner and stabilizes clusters of PCP complexes. We identify a previously unknown function for the oligomerizing Dishevelled/Axin (DIX) domain of Dvl3, typically associated with Wnt signaling, in Dvl3 asymmetric localization. These observations underscore a role for Dvl oligomerization in assembly and stabilization of asymmetric PCP puncta.

articles_hidden.title: Contagion-preserving compression for multiscale epidemic modeling
articles_hidden.authors: Leyang Xue, Zengru Di, An Zeng
articles_hidden.abstract: Understanding how contagion unfolds on large, heterogeneous networks is essential for predicting and controlling spreading processes, yet structural complexity often obscures the mechanisms governing transmission across scales. Here, we show that contagion is naturally organized around dense local structures that become dynamical spreading units once infection saturates within them. Building on this principle, we introduce iterative structural coarse-graining (ISCG), a framework that compresses large networks into interpretable multiscale representations while retaining the contagion dynamics of the original system. In this saturation regime, these representations reproduce macroscopic outbreak sizes, node-level infection risks, and spatiotemporal infection trajectories across scales. Beyond this regime, ISCG enables controlled trade-offs between dynamical fidelity and structural compression. The resulting multiscale representations support mechanism-driven intervention strategies, including influence maximization, immunization, and surveillance, that consistently outperform adaptive centrality–based methods. These results establish a general multiscale framework for representing, understanding, and controlling contagion in networked systems.

articles_hidden.title: Effects of probiotics on joint homeostasis and osteoarthritis: Development of microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip
articles_hidden.authors: Jun Liu, Ning Zhang, Yiting Lei, Xiaoshuai Wang, Xiang Zhang, Wei Huang, Changhai Ding, Denghui Xie, Jun Yu, Rocky S. Tuan, Zhong Alan Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Although emerging evidence implicates gut microbiome-cartilage cross-talk in the pathogenesis of osteoarthritis (OA), the most common joint disease, studying this microbe-gut-joint axis remains challenging due to limitations of animal models and conventional in vitro systems. Here, we report a microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip (MGCAoC) that recreates tissue-specific microenvironments with oxygen gradients and physiological fluid shear. The computer simulation–optimized chip design generates an anoxic-oxic interface for the gut module and enables perfusion of probiotic metabolites to human cartilage organoids without cross-contamination. Multiomics profiling suggested that probiotic metabolites may promote cartilage anabolism, potentially involving PI3K and MAPK pathway, and this effect was associated with up-regulated collagen type II and aggrecan expression while suppressing metalloproteinases. In inflamed cartilage organoids, these metabolites were associated with reduced proinflammatory signaling while preserving matrix integrity. The chondroprotective effects were confirmed using cartilage organoids derived from patients with OA treated with identified metabolites. This MGCAoC enables mechanistic investigation of gut-joint axis physiology and provides a versatile preclinical tool for screening probiotic-based OA therapeutics.

articles_hidden.title: Buffaloed in Brandenburg: Germany’s first brush with foot-and-mouth disease after four decades of freedom
articles_hidden.authors: Michael Eschbaumer, Christoph Staubach, Florian Pfaff, Jörn Gethmann, Katja Schulz, Lisa Rogoll, Sabine Bock, Wulf-Iwo Bock, Christoph Schulze, Ronny Marquart, Nicole Reinhardt, Stephan Nickisch, Nadine Kakerow, Sabrina Freter, Annett Rudovsky, Kerstin Albrecht, Sandra Leo, Christina Haarmann, Sarah Lenz, Barbara Hoffmann, Sten Calvelage, Dirk Höper, Patrick Zitzow, Angele Breithaupt, Can Çokçalişkan, Ünal Parlak, Sharon Karniely, Laith Mohammed Salih Abdulrasool, Nick Knowles, Guillaume Girault, Aurore Romey, Labib Bakkali Kassimi, Donald P. King, Christa Kühn, Carola Sauter-Louis, Martin Beer
articles_hidden.abstract: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) virus is one of the most feared and most consequential pathogens of livestock worldwide. It can be spread rapidly by the transboundary movement of animals, animal products, and by-products. In January 2025, Germany detected its first FMD outbreak since 1988 in extensively reared water buffalo on a small farm in the state of Brandenburg, directly outside Berlin, the federal capital. Immediate control measures including a standstill for movements of susceptible animals and pre-emptive culling were implemented by the veterinary authorities. Whole-genome sequencing identified the virus as serotype O, topotype ME-SA, lineage SA-2018 and revealed extensive recombination, but cross-neutralization assays suggested good heterologous protection by an O/PanAsia-2 vaccine strain. Epidemiological back-calculation placed the time of virus introduction in late December 2024. Although the entry route remains unresolved, human-associated introduction is most likely. Network analysis revealed minimal farm connectivity, and simulations predicted low potential for onward transmission, which is consistent with the outbreak being ultimately restricted to a single herd. This event underscores the constant and unpredictable risk of introduction of the virus. Early detection through increased awareness and comprehensive differential diagnostics as well as the international collaboration of veterinary services, laboratories, and experts are essential in the face of the global presence of FMD.

articles_hidden.title: Global conservation additionality hindered by persisting fishing pressure in marine protected areas
articles_hidden.authors: Millenne Ohanna, Juliette Jacquemont, Joachim Claudet
articles_hidden.abstract: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are the cornerstone of global marine conservation strategies. Yet, their capacity to achieve conservation gains (i.e., conservation additionality) hinges on the decrease in human threats to biodiversity within their boundary, a feature rarely measured or reported. Here, we test a central but underexamined question in global conservation policy: Have MPA implementations actually reduced within-boundary fishing pressure, currently the main direct human threat to marine biodiversity? Using a stratified before-after-control-impact approach, we investigated 861 MPAs of varying levels of protection across all ocean basins, representing half of global MPA coverage, and found that most implementations were not followed by decreases in industrial fishing effort. Protection levels strongly predicted the direction and magnitude of relative changes in fishing effort after implementation. Only fully protected areas were associated with significant decreases in fishing effort within boundaries. Highly protected areas were only associated with lower rates of increase in fishing effort within compared to outside boundaries. Both fully and highly protected areas were implemented in areas experiencing initial low fishing effort, reducing the overall abatement in fishing effort achieved. Conversely, areas with higher initial fishing effort tended to be attributed to MPAs with low levels of protection, also limiting abatement. Larger MPAs were associated with greater decreases in fishing effort, while time since implementation had no significant effect. Complementing targets of protection coverage and protection levels with conservation additionality targets, such as pressure abatement, could shift incentives from quantity to effectiveness of interventions and ensure positive biodiversity conservation outcomes.

articles_hidden.title: Divergent demographic responses to the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic catastrophe in mid-Holocene Japan
articles_hidden.authors: Enrico R. Crema, Mitsuhiro Kuwahata, Junzo Uchiyama, Ari Junno, Felix Riede, Peter D. Jordan
articles_hidden.abstract: We examine human demographic responses to one of the Holocene’s largest volcanic eruptions, which devastated East Asia 7300 years ago. Archaeologists have intensively debated the impacts of massive environmental shocks, highlighting either societal collapse or cultural continuity, although few studies situate such catastrophic events within longer-term demographic trajectories. We address this gap in knowledge by using statistical models to infer the demographic and environmental impacts of the Kikai-Akahoya (K-Ah) eruption on Jomon foraging communities occupying the Japanese archipelago. Traditionally framed as an apocalyptic “forcing” mechanism that changed the direction of Japanese prehistory, our results identify a more complex and contingent suite of demographic outcomes. Although we do find evidence of major population collapse in immediately adjacent regions to the volcano, some proximal populations actually increased after the catastrophe, whereas some distal communities were affected by environmental consequences that have hitherto been overlooked. Demographic perspectives on ancient disasters are useful in generating a deeper understanding of the contingent ways in which cultures and societies cope with sudden shocks and catastrophes.

articles_hidden.title: Radical-induced autoxidation dominates squalene oxidative aging under environmental conditions
articles_hidden.authors: Xinke Wang, Jillian P. Downey, Giulia Gobbi, William D. Fahy, Wanqi Wu, Linna Xie, Xingwang Hou, Hui Peng, Jonathan P. D. Abbatt
articles_hidden.abstract: Ozone has been viewed as the principal oxidant of skin oils and other unsaturated surface films, but their fate under realistic indoor conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use squalene (SQ), a major component of skin lipids, to investigate the dominant oxidation pathways in occupied indoor environments and laboratory flow reactors. With exposure to indoor air, SQ decay and reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation accelerated over time, consistent with autoxidation. Laboratory experiments with ozone alone drove first-order SQ loss and humidity-dependent emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). In contrast, exposure to both ozone and • OH produced nonexponential SQ decays, higher ROS yields, a much stronger in-film • OH source, and condensed-phase products enriched in highly oxidized organic hydroperoxides that closely match those observed indoors. Unexpectedly, gas-phase • OH strongly suppressed VOC emissions. These results demonstrate that gas-phase radical-induced autoxidation governs SQ aging, challenging the prevailing ozone-centric view of indoor skin oil oxidation.

articles_hidden.title: Rapid coral bleaching recovery via symbiont transfer from healthy corals
articles_hidden.authors: Daniel S. Collins, Jana Sipkova, Nathaniel R. Mollica, Thomas Rolander, Courtney N. Klepac, Gabriel F. Calistro, Vanessa Barone, Fiorenza Micheli, Stephen R. Palumbi
articles_hidden.abstract: Coral bleaching, the temperature-induced loss of dinoflagellate symbionts, is a major driver of global coral reef decline. Although corals can regain symbionts through repopulation of residual symbionts or via environmental acquisition, these processes are often too slow to prevent coral mortality. Mechanisms that enable rapid and effective symbiont reintroduction leading to full recovery remain largely unknown. Here, we demonstrate coral bleaching recovery through contact-mediated transfer of symbionts from healthy corals using small coral fragments. We show that symbiont transfer is rapid, occurring over days to weeks, and highly efficient, with only brief physical contact with healthy corals required. A single week of contact, and in some cases as few as 3 days, provides sufficient symbionts to initiate sustained and full self-recovery. By 1 week, symbiont population doubling time is approximately 4 days, up to an order of magnitude faster than most recovery times for corals in the field. We identify tissue fusion as the mechanism enabling directional symbiont transfer from healthy to bleached coral tissue. As a result, contact-dependent recovery is restricted to corals of the same genet, whereas heterologous genet pairings trigger antagonistic interactions. However, symbiont transfer via polyp uptake occurs immediately upon contact in both same-genet and mixed-genet pairings, revealing an additional, slower pathway for symbiont transfer that is insufficient on its own to support colony recovery. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized natural process for efficiently reintroducing symbionts to bleached corals, providing a foundation for research into potential recovery interventions.

articles_hidden.title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization
articles_hidden.authors: Matthieu Pierre Platre, Lukas Brent, Matias F. Gleason, Preyanka Mehta, Ling Zhang, Laia Armengot, Julie Neveu, Olivier Kaakeh, Min Cao, Laura M. Martins, Julie A. Law, Santosh B. Satbhai, Nuria S. Coll, Marc Valls, Grégory Vert, Wolfgang Busch
articles_hidden.abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Together, our findings uncover a fast-acting iron homeostasis pathway in plants that dynamically couples nutrient availability with immunity, thereby shaping host microbe interactions at the onset of infection.

articles_hidden.title: Highlights from an early base camp in Beringia 13,800 years ago: Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ and the Late Pleistocene peopling of Alaska
articles_hidden.authors: Kelly E. Graf, Ted Goebel, Aureáde Henry, Bryan Hockett, Nathan Shelley, Mariya Antonosyan, Julie Meachen, Mason Sewing, Mia Harbort, Julie A. Esdale, Sarah A. Allaun, Angela K. Gore, Jeffrey T. Rasic, Patrick Roberts, Evelynn Combs, Donald Charlie
articles_hidden.abstract: Human dispersal across the Bering Land Bridge (BLB) was a key event in the peopling of the Americas, but Beringia’s archaeological record remains poorly understood. In response, the Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ site in interior Alaska has been the focus of a multi-disciplinary study since 2016. The site contains three archaeological components dating to the Late Pleistocene, 13.8, 13, and 12.7 thousand years ago. The oldest component yielded an expressive array of cultural remains, including a unique hafted-biface form, osseous tools, diverse fauna, and well-preserved activity areas, a record unparalleled for this age in Beringia. Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ represents the earliest known Nenana Complex occupation east of the BLB, and its distinct hafted-biface form occurs in coeval sites west of the BLB, providing an important trans-Beringian cultural link. Although not Beringia’s oldest site, Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ reveals important information about Late Glacial peopling and settling-in behavior in this far northern setting.

articles_hidden.title: Ocean circulation changes rather than global warming drove temperature trends across the Miocene Climatic Optimum
articles_hidden.authors: Evi Wubben, Xiaoqing Liu, Tjerk J. T. Veenstra, R. Paul Acosta, Joyce den Hollander, Chris Overduin, Matthew Huber, Francesca Sangiorgi, Francien Peterse, Appy Sluijs
articles_hidden.abstract: Early-to-Middle Miocene [23 to 13.8 million years ago (Ma)] climates were ∼6° to 9°C warmer than today. Around 16.9 Ma, benthic foraminiferal oxygen isotope (δ 18 O) records suggest pronounced warming, known as the Miocene Climatic Optimum (MCO) onset. However, explaining this putative global warming with carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) forcing faces challenges in terms of timing and forcing magnitude. Our new biomarker-based ocean temperature records, combined with published data, reveal no substantial mean global upper ocean warming across the MCO. Instead, temperature changes differ considerably between sites, with some regions showing cooling. Climate model sensitivity tests indicate that these patterns are best explained by ocean circulation changes, likely due to gateway changes and Antarctic ice sheet variations. This suggests that the MCO signature is better attributed to ocean circulation changes rather than a CO 2 -driven global warming event. The δ 18 O signal therefore represents warmer deepwater sourcing and/or reduced Antarctic glacial volume, resolving the longstanding challenge of explaining MCO warming without a pronounced CO 2 rise.

articles_hidden.title: Seabirds and native vegetation drive ecosystem processes that support atoll island resilience
articles_hidden.authors: Nicholas A. J. Graham, Cassandra E. Benkwitt, Ines D. Lange, Chris T. Perry, Eleanor R. Thomson, Lisa M. Wedding, Ruth E. Dunn, Sebastian Steibl, Courtney E. Stuart, Laura-Li Jeannot, Jennifer Appoo, Julia Rodriguez Fillol, Marleen Stuhr, Pirta Palola, Peter Carr, Jayna L. DeVore, Simon Ducatez, Anna Zora, Ayla K. Hastings, Solène Fabre Barroso, Sean Evans, Melissa Schulze, Emma Cotton, Hazel Reddington, Yadvinder Malhi
articles_hidden.abstract: Ecosystem restoration is expected to enhance ecosystem resilience to climate change, but few empirical and mechanistic demonstrations of such assertions exist. Here, we explore this topic for tropical atoll systems, combining science on nutrient subsidies and geo-ecological functions through a unifying ecological energetics lens. We show that native forest cover and seabird nutrient inputs increase primary productivity and secondary metabolism on islands and adjacent coral reefs, scaling with key ecosystem processes. We then demonstrate that seabird and native forest restoration could contribute to reducing island climate change vulnerability by (i) increasing reef accretion rates such that they keep pace with sea-level rise under a 2.0°C warming scenario, (ii) enhancing the production rate of sediment, which could contribute to island maintenance, and (iii) increasing vegetation fine root length, aiding island sediment stabilization. Collectively, our findings provide an integrated energetics and geo-ecological perspective that suggests rewilding of atolls can contribute to climate resilience.

articles_hidden.title: Immune biomarkers of response and resistance to ipilimumab and nivolumab in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
articles_hidden.authors: Apostolia M. Tsimberidou, Christopher R. Cabanski, Alexandra Drakaki, Danny N. Khalil, Bilal A. Siddiqui, Sreyashi Basu, Kwame Okrah, Diane M. Da Silva, Shikha Gautam, Farah A. Alayli, Mike Schachter, Justin Fairchild, Wai Chin Foo, Silvia Boffo, Jamie Arnott, Ute Dugan, Sumit K. Subudhi, Padmanee Sharma
articles_hidden.abstract: Immune checkpoint therapies have shown limited efficacy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The AMADEUS prostate expansion cohort (NCT03651271) evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biomarkers of escalating ipilimumab doses combined with nivolumab. Patients received ipilimumab 1 milligram per kilogram (mg/kg) + nivolumab 360 mg (I1+N360), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I3+N1), or ipilimumab 5 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I5+N1). Coprimary endpoints were 6-month disease control rate (DCR) and changes in tumoral CD8 percentage. Thirty-two patients were enrolled. DCRs were 33% (4 of 12) for I1+N360, 20% (1 of 5) for I3+N1, and 20% (3 of 15) for I5+N1. Across cohorts, tumoral CD8 percentage increased by a median of 5.0%. Although higher ipilimumab doses were tolerable, I1+N360 achieved similar disease control and immune activation with a more favorable safety profile. Early disease progression was associated with increased expression of a TREM2-associated myeloid gene signature, which was also significantly enriched in two independent prostate cancer datasets.

articles_hidden.title: Sustainable solar water purification: Exploring the structural advantages of higher plants
articles_hidden.authors: Xue Han, Chuxin Lei, Mingyue Miao, Chunlei Zhang, Yingying Zhang, Yiqiang Wu, Huaiyan Li, Yating Wang, Mengjiao Shi, Qing Li, Haipeng Yu, Shouxin Liu, Jian Li, Wenshuai Chen, Guihua Yu
articles_hidden.abstract: Solar vapor generation is a promising technique for water purification, although the development of efficient and sustainable systems for practical use remains challenging. Here, we introduce a higher plant–derived evaporator, leveraging the structural advantages of plants and the synergistic integration of multiple components, including carbon black–coated ultrathin wood slices with perforated pores, nanocellulose aerogel, and vertically aligned wheat straws. This configuration facilitates low-tortuosity water transport within the internal framework while promoting interfacial evaporation at its surface. Under 1 sun, the evaporator achieved an evaporation rate of up to 3.2 kilograms per square meter (kg m −2 ) per hour. The material’s scalability and the capability to continuously collect clean water in outdoor environments were successfully demonstrated. Outdoors, under a solar intensity of 0.5 to 0.9 sun, the assembled device achieved a daily fresh water yield of up to 10.9 kg m −2 from seawater. With highly accessible renewable raw materials, low production cost, and exceptional water purification efficiency, this cost-effective solar evaporator is edge closer to viable, real-world applications.

articles_hidden.title: A transcriptional cofactor GRIP1 drives PPARγ DNA binding and p300-dependent enhancer activity during homeostatic macrophage polarization
articles_hidden.authors: Marija Dacic, William J Stein, Ruoxi Yuan, Dinesh K Deochand, Joshua K Morrison, Ketsia Seide, Yurii Chinenov, Inez Rogatsky
articles_hidden.abstract: Homeostatic macrophages maintain tissue health and resolve inflammation. Upon sustained exposure to type II cytokine IL4, transcription factors STAT6, KLF4, EGR2 and a ligand-regulated nuclear receptor PPARγ orchestrate the M2 IL4 ‘polarization’, marked by enhancer RNA (eRNA) production near multiple M2 genes. The mechanisms of enhancer activation by unliganded PPARγ are poorly understood. We interrogated cofactor requirements for PPARγ-driven gene expression in M2 IL4 , including those lacking PPARγ or a ligand-dependent nuclear receptor coregulator NCoA2/GRIP1 vs. macrophages treated with the PPARγ agonist rosiglitazone. As expected, rosiglitazone activated conventional PPARγ targets; GRIP1 deletion blunted their induction and depleted GRIP1-interacting histone acetyltransferase p300 from PPARγ-bound sites. Surprisingly, GRIP1 colocalized with unliganded PPARγ in M0 and M2 IL4 , and GRIP1 ablation dramatically reduced genome-wide DNA binding of PPARγ itself while promoting broad deposition of CTCF insulator. Functionally, GRIP1 deletion mirrored PPARγ deficiency, establishing GRIP1 as a central regulator of unliganded PPARγ DNA binding, required for both eRNA and mRNA transcription of PPARγ targets in homeostatic macrophages.

articles_hidden.title: Citron kinase activity controls alternative splicing events that drive prostate cancer growth
articles_hidden.authors: Chitra Rawat, Nidhi Singh, Ujjwal R. Dahiya, Qiang Hu, Sarah Ng, Dingxiao Zhang, Shaun R. Stauffer, Amina Zoubeidi, Eva Corey, Jesse McKenney, Christopher J. Weight, Samuel C. Haywood, Song Liu, Tao Liu, Hannelore V. Heemers
articles_hidden.abstract: Prostate cancer (CaP) remains a major cause of cancer death in men, underscoring the need for mechanistically novel therapies. We previously identified the action of the mitotic kinase citron (CIT) kinase as a key driver of CaP progression and promising therapeutic target, but selective CIT inhibitors are not available. We therefore asked whether a better understanding of the action of CIT substrates, which execute CIT kinase action in CaP cells, can lead to novel approaches and/or alternative targets to indirectly interfere with CIT’s activity during CaP progression. In view of the enrichment in functions in alternative splicing among CIT substrates, we focus on the RNA splicing regulator THRAP3 as a representative substrate. Direct THRAP3 phosphorylation by CIT determined THRAP3’s RNA binding to CIT-controlled pre–messenger RNA targets. Cross-linking and immunoprecipitation sequencing identified a subset of CIT-dependent THRAP3-bound genes that were preferentially involved in cell proliferation. THRAP3 RNA binding was enriched in genes that undergo alternative splicing during CaP progression. CIT-dependent THRAP3-bound transcripts stimulated the growth of CaP cell lines, xenografts, patient-derived organoids, and patient-derived xenograft (PDX)–derived organoids, whereas CIT-independent THRAP3-bound transcripts from the same gene did not. An antisense oligo that blocks THRAP3’s recruitment to a CIT-dependent RNA binding site prevented the production of CIT- and THRAP3-dependent transcripts and inhibited the growth of cell lines and PDX-derived organoids representing different CaP stages and lineages but not of benign cells. Thus, CIT-mediated alternative splicing drives CaP progression, and its inhibition is a new therapeutic strategy in treatment-resistant CaP.

articles_hidden.title: Long-term immunoprophylaxis by TLR9 ligand mediates macrophage-ILC cross-talk against respiratory viral infection
articles_hidden.authors: Asuka Joy Tobuse, Kouji Kobiyama, Jun Tsuchida, Masamitsu N. Asaka, Daichi Utsumi, Mariana Silva Almeida, Yaeko Nakajima-Takagi, Motohiko Oshima, Tomoya Hayashi, Burcu Temizoz, Etsushi Kuroda, Cevayir Coban, Yasuhiro Yasutomi, Atsushi Iwama, Ken J. Ishii
articles_hidden.abstract: Rapid development of host immunity is critical during the emergence of viral outbreaks when vaccines are not yet available. Here, we demonstrate that CpG oligodeoxynucleotide-schizophyllan complex (K3-SPG) induces antigen-independent, long-term protection against lethal respiratory virus infection. A single intranasal administration successfully enhanced host resistance to infection for as long as 100 days posttreatment. Mechanistically, we observed a lung-restricted biphasic innate activation of macrophages and innate lymphoid cells. Early protection was mediated by CD11b + CD11c + macrophages (DP MΦ) and monocyte-derived interstitial macrophages (IMΦ). Late protection was mediated by innate lymphoid cells that were epigenetically reprogrammed, suggesting that two distinct innate immune subsets contribute to the maintenance of disease tolerance in the lung microenvironment. Deficiency of TLR9 or TNF-α abrogated innate activation and protective immunity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that adjuvant-induced prophylaxis is a promising approach to enhancing host resistance against respiratory virus infection, involving the biphasic cooperation between innate immune cells in the local tissue.

articles_hidden.title: Observation of electrically generated polaron-polaritons in a monolayer MoSe 2 microcavity
articles_hidden.authors: Yuanjun Guan, Mengyao Xu, Zhen Cui, Xingzhou Chen, Chengye Ding, Xiaoqing Zhou, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Jesper Levinsen, Meera M. Parish, Pavlos G. Savvidis, Zhe-Yu Shi, Zheng Sun, Jian Wu
articles_hidden.abstract: Quasiparticles arising from the interaction between mobile impurities and a quantum many-body environment—known as polarons—play a pivotal role in shaping the optical and electronic properties of low-dimensional systems. Here, we report the direct observation of electrically generated polaron-polaritons within a monolayer molybdenum diselenide microcavity. By embedding the monolayer in a planar optical cavity, we achieve strong coupling between exciton-polarons and cavity photons, creating an electrically driven light-emitting diode based on polaron-polaritons. The device exhibits an external quantum efficiency of ∼0.15%, representing a 10-fold enhancement over prior exciton-polariton devices based on monolayer tungsten disulfide. This demonstration establishes a versatile platform for inversionless laser technology and for polariton-based quantum optoelectronics while offering insights into radiative many-body physics in two-dimensional semiconductors.

articles_hidden.title: Intensification of East Asian summer extreme precipitation under a net-zero anthropogenic CO 2 emission scenario
articles_hidden.authors: Seungmok Paik, Daehyun Kim, Soon-Il An, So-Eun Park, Andrew D. King, Seung-Ki Min, Chao Liu, Jongsoo Shin
articles_hidden.abstract: Global warming has intensified extreme precipitation, a trend projected to continue as warming persists. However, how extreme precipitation characteristics respond to global warming mitigation strategies remains poorly understood. This study examines East Asian summer extreme precipitation responses under a net-zero anthropogenic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emission scenario. Despite substantial cooling over East Asia following atmospheric CO 2 concentration decline, the intensity of extreme precipitation events continues to increase for about 30 years and does not subsequently weaken. This counterintuitive result arises mainly from intensified upward motion during extreme precipitation events, driven by enhanced baroclinicity and strengthening of the upper-tropospheric jet, which together overcompensate the cooling effect. These are essentially due to the hysteresis in the Atlantic (i.e., Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation slowdown), Southern (i.e., sustained warming), and Pacific (i.e., El Niño–like warming) Oceans. Our findings highlight that achieving net-zero anthropogenic CO 2 emissions is insufficient to mitigate intensifying extreme rainfall events in the densely populated East Asian countries.

articles_hidden.title: ALIX-dependent small extracellular vesicles from tissue-resident mesenchymal cells regulate pancreatic β cell proliferation in obesity
articles_hidden.authors: Yuhei Uehara, Hirofumi Nagao, Aoki Tobimatsu, Keitaro Kawada, Shunsuke Shiode, Emi Horitani, Yoshinari Obata, Shiro Fukuda, Yuya Fujishima, Shunbun Kita, Hitoshi Nishizawa, Iichiro Shimomura
articles_hidden.abstract: Cells throughout the body release small extracellular vesicles (sEVs), including exosomes, that function as modulators of both local and systemic metabolism. Using mice in which ALIX, a key regulator of sEV biogenesis, was selectively deleted in PDGFRα + mesenchymal progenitors (Pα-ALIXKO mice), we demonstrate a critical role for mesenchymal sEV production in metabolic regulation. In high-fat diet–induced obesity, Pα-ALIXKO mice exhibited reduced weight gain and smaller subcutaneous adipocytes compared with control mice. Despite similar insulin sensitivity, these mice showed impaired glucose tolerance, which was associated with reduced pancreatic β cell area and smaller islets. sEVs isolated from conditioned media of knockout (KO)–derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) exhibited a reduced capacity to promote β cell proliferation. Furthermore, MSCs isolated from subcutaneous adipose tissue of KO mice showed elevated mRNA expression of inflammatory genes. Together, these findings indicate that ALIX in tissue-resident mesenchymal progenitors is required for pancreatic β cell proliferation and glucose homeostasis in obesity.

articles_hidden.title: Spectral tuning and signaling of diverse and far red–sensitive rhodopsins in mantis shrimp eyes
articles_hidden.authors: Camille Brouillon, Alina Pushkarev, Marjorie A. Liénard, Songhwan Hwang, Arno Munhoven, Richard McDowell, Robert J. Lucas, Megan Porter, Han Sun, Peter Hegemann
articles_hidden.abstract: Stomatopod crustaceans (mantis shrimps) have extraordinary eyes with unmatched visual rhodopsin diversity, but their potential for broad color detection remains unclear. Here, we report that 17 rhodopsins, mostly from the midband eye region, are involved in color sensing and functionally diverse signaling via Gq/Gi coupling and describe the underlying mechanisms of spectral tuning. Two mid-wavelength rhodopsins preferentially absorb blue light and a majority of long-wavelength opsins absorb in the green range, but three absorb light beyond 600 nanometers, representing exquisite far red–sensitive animal rhodopsins. Several blue and red rhodopsins exhibit photoreversibility with opposite spectral shifts explained by retinal binding interactions, revealing unrecognized photochemical flexibility in stomatopod photoreception. Row-specific spectral sensitivity results from combining carotenoid filters with multiple individually tuned rhodopsins, altogether extending broad vision to the far-red spectrum.

articles_hidden.title: Local control of Cre-regulated genetic modeling in vivo using wireless implantable optoelectronics
articles_hidden.authors: Trisha Bansal, Min-Kyu Lee, Courtney Coleman, Young-Mee Kim, Dane Hintermueller, Yaner Chen, Varsha Sreekanth, Chad R. Haney, Olga A. Karginova, Raudel Avila, Jacob Matsche, Shaluah Vijeth, Farah Yousef, Kento Yamagishi, Jiheon Kang, Kaitlyn Mowry, Minsung Kim, Sophianne Loh, Sachin Clark, Huong Huynh, Youngdo Kim, Kaiqing Zhang, Haohui Zhang, Shupeng Li, Yuanting Wei, Steve Seung-Young Lee, Yuru Liu, Anthony R. Banks, Odile David, Peter T. Toth, Yonggang Huang, Ameen Salahudeen, Cameron H. Good, Jalees Rehman, John A. Rogers, Andrei V. Karginov
articles_hidden.abstract: Effective modeling of chronic human diseases in vivo requires precise spatiotemporal regulation of molecular processes at defined tissue locations. Optogenetic and optoelectronic tools can provide such control but targeting internal organs such as the lungs remain challenging. To address this, we developed E-LightR-Cre recombinase, enabling precise, spatially restricted gene activation with no dark-state activity and robust blue light responsiveness. To achieve local activation of E-LightR-Cre in specific organ sites, we engineered wireless, fully implantable optoelectronic devices enabling focal illumination of murine lungs with no discernible organ damage. The size of the activated area is controlled by modulating light intensity and duration. Using implanted optoelectronic devices, we activated E-LightR-Cre in a selected area of mouse lungs and achieved local regulation of targeted genes. Light-regulated expression of the oncogenic KRas-G12D mutant in mouse lungs induced local formation of oncogenic lesions. These results show that our protein engineering and adaptable optoelectronic approaches enable facile application of optogenetic tools for locally controlled disease modeling in vivo.

articles_hidden.title: Reduced organic nitrogen compounds dominate the toxicity of PM 2.5 organics following internal exposure
articles_hidden.authors: Yaling Zeng, Xin Yang, Xin Yuan, Rongrong Xu, Ke Yang, Baixin Zhang, Jinghao Zhai, Baohua Cai, Shao Shi, Yin Zhang, Yujie Zhang, Ziting Hou, Antai Zhang, Zhenxing Shen, Tzung-May Fu, Lei Zhu, Huizhong Shen, Jianhuai Ye, Chen Wang, Shu Tao
articles_hidden.abstract: Atmospheric fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) remains a major global health risk, with its associated health burden continuing to rise despite decades of pollution control efforts. Air pollution studies often focus on particle levels and known toxins, missing hidden organics that may drive serious health risks. Here, we conducted a comprehensive molecular and toxicological investigation of urban atmospheric particles, integrating nontargeted analysis of high-resolution mass spectrometry, protein adductomics–based internal exposure assessment, and multi-endpoint toxicity prediction. We find reduced organic nitrogen (RON) compounds as the predominant drivers of the toxicity of the internal exposed particle-bound organic fraction. RON account for 39% of total multi-organ toxicity, exceeding the 23% contribution from traditionally emphasized oxygenated organics. RON compounds exhibit strong binding affinity to human serum albumin, facilitating systemic distribution and toxic effects across respiratory, neurological, hepatic, renal, and hematological endpoints. Our findings identify RON as a key driver of organic PM 2.5 toxicity via internal exposure pathways and highlight the urgent need to regulate reactive nitrogen species.

articles_hidden.title: Phage-ICE tandems facilitate bacterial adaptation and antimicrobial resistance spread
articles_hidden.authors: Jinhu Huang, Jiaqi Zhao, Pengchao Zhan, Xingyang Dai, Xinming Pan, Zhenmiao Li, Wenbin Zhao, Xiaoli Shi, Xiaoming Wang, Shengyong Mao, Jiale Ma, Liping Wang, Jinxin Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: Phages and integrative and conjugative elements (ICEs) drive bacterial evolution, but how their interplay shapes bacterial adaptation and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dissemination remains unclear. Here, we characterize phage-ICE tandems formed by site-specific accretion of phages and ICEs into cotransferable units. In Streptococcus , phage-encoded integrases (IntIE Phage ) drive stress-inducible excision and circularization, after which ICE machinery mediates conduction of the tandem. When excision is impaired, phage and phage-ICE fragments disseminate by transformation and integrate via RecA-dependent homologous recombination (HR), providing a fail-safe route. This pathway enables cotransfer of flanking chromosomal DNA, generating length-variable integrations that remodel transcriptional programs and increase oxidative stress tolerance. A global screen identified 612 phage-ICE tandems across seven phyla and 135 species, including multidrug-resistant pathogens, with lineage-specific repertoires of AMR, virulence, and metabolic genes. Rather than a hybrid element, these structures represent functional interplay where prophages exploit ICE conjugation while facilitating mobilization of the composite region. By coupling excision, transfer, and recombination, phage-ICEs shape adaptation and accelerate AMR spread.

articles_hidden.title: A neuronal GPCR modifies neuropeptide signaling to suppress proteostasis in distal tissues
articles_hidden.authors: Joud Hirbawi, Adam Zaretsky, Huadong Zhu, Uri Goshtchevsky, Gourab Dey, Emmanuelle Merquiol, Atif Ahmed Siddiqui, Irit Cohen, Galia Blum, Ehud Cohen
articles_hidden.abstract: The proteostasis network (PN) safeguards the integrity of proteins by promoting various cellular activities. However, with aging, the PN’s competence declines and aggregated proteins accrue within cells. This process underlies the development of neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer’s and Huntington’s diseases. While the PN functions within cells, proteostasis is regulated across the organism by intertissue communication, which is partially governed by neurons. We previously found that reducing the expression of gtr-1 , which encodes a neuronal heterotrimeric guanine nucleotide–binding protein–coupled receptor, mitigates the toxicity of the Alzheimer’s disease cause, Aβ peptide. Here, we investigated the mechanism that is acted upon the knockdown of gtr-1 and found that it differentially modulates gene expression profiles, including of neuropeptide-coding genes, and dissimilarly modifies protein aggregation in worms that express distinct proteotoxic proteins. The knockdown of gtr-1 also enhances protein degradation. These findings highlight the roles of neuropeptides as organismal coordinators of proteostasis in the face of distinct proteotoxic challenges.

articles_hidden.title: A “Progenitor Cell Ark” hydrogel system for intervertebral disc regeneration via mitochondrial targeting and mitophagy enhancement
articles_hidden.authors: Yilin Yang, Yixue Huang, Hao Liu, Jiangbo Guo, Haifei Cao, Qin Shi, Yong Xu, Huilin Yang
articles_hidden.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), driven by progenitor cell loss and oxidative stress, remains a major clinical challenge with limited effective regenerative therapies. Here, we present a “Progenitor Cell Ark,” a triple-layered hydrogel microsphere system designed for synergistic cell delivery and microenvironment remediation. The Ark comprises an outer nucleus pulposus progenitor cell (NPPC) layer for cell replenishment, a middle GelMA/HAMA scaffold for support, and an inner SS31-modified ultrasmall Prussian blue nanozyme (SS31-UPN) layer that specifically targets mitochondria to scavenge ROS and promote mitophagy. In vitro, SS31-UPN effectively protected NPPCs from oxidative damage, restored mitochondrial function, and enhanced mitophagy. Critically, in severe IVDD rat models, the Progenitor Cell Ark significantly improved intervertebral disc structure, promoted neo-tissue formation, and restored biomechanical function, outperforming cell or bioscaffold therapy alone. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that SS31-UPN’s mitochondrial targeting enhances mitophagy, drives ECM and energy metabolic remodeling, and preserves NPPC stemness, thereby creating a proregenerative milieu. This integrated “cell-in-a-box” strategy offers a robust platform for reversing IVDD and holds notable translational potential for regenerative medicine.

articles_hidden.title: Nanoconfinement-cooperated catalysis enables rapid tandem redox kinetics for wide-temperature lithium-sulfur batteries
articles_hidden.authors: Tianli Li, Tao Chen, Pu Hu, Congcong Cai, Juntao Wang, Chaoqun Shang, Liwei Xiong, Yajie Li, Hanxing Liu, Jian Wang, Yaobing Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: The slow kinetics of sulfur cathodes caused by the high energy barriers of Li + desolvation stem primarily from the structure of the inner Helmholtz plane (IHP). Herein, a synergistic strategy combining electrochemical tandem catalysis with spatial nanoconfinement is proposed to regulate the Li(solvent) x + dynamics. As a proof-of-concept, the porous covalent organic framework (denoted as TPBD) decorated MXene is in situ constructed, acting as a tandem kinetic promoter. The theoretical simulations and in situ Raman reveal that the porous TPBD layer confines the bulky Li(solvent) x + species and sieves the spatial structure with accelerated Li + diffusion kinetics. Meanwhile, MXene serves as a negatively charged substrate that helps disrupt anion-solvent interactions and reconstruct the solvation structure at the IHP, thereby enhancing Li + kinetics and sulfur redox reversibility. Encouragingly, the assembled cells demonstrate a superior Li + transference number (0.77), long-term cycling lifespan up to 1000 cycles, as well as excellent areal capacity (>6 mAh cm −2 ) at 0°C and superior rate capability at 50°C under a high sulfur loading of 7.51 mg cm −2 . The as-prepared pouch cell remains stable for over 100 cycles, validating this novel integration of catalysis and nanoconfinement for tandem kinetics in Li-S batteries.

articles_hidden.title: Multidegree fluorescence–optical rotatory dispersion (F-ORD) from submonolayer interfacial chiral films
articles_hidden.authors: Kevin Murati, Matthew R. Wilson, Isabela Capelozi de Freitas, TJ Pinedo, Benjamin W. Cerjan, Patrizia Polichetti, Alexander J. Higgins, Ethan T. Cox, Osama Abuhammad, Lyudmila V. Slipchenko, Garth J. Simpson
articles_hidden.abstract: Homochiral monomolecular thin films adsorbed to fused silica produced fluorescence–optical rotatory dispersion (F-ORD; i.e., optical rotation of the fluorescence emission relative to the excitation beam) more than seven orders of magnitude greater than anticipated by conventional origins of optical rotatory dispersion (i.e., optical rotation of the excitation beam after passing through a chiral film relative to its initial plane of polarization). Optical rotation of −4.5 ± 0.5° was observed in the principal axis of fluorescence emission relative to that of excitation for submonolayer dip-coated thin films of (S)-naproxen, with the sign of the rotation inverting for comparable films of (R)-naproxen. The chiral-specific F-ORD response was nonreciprocal, inverting in sign upon flipping of the sample orientation (i.e., source-facing versus detector-facing), suggesting selectivity to chiral molecules oriented at the interface. The interface selectivity, chiral selectivity, and large magnitude of the response were in excellent agreement with a fully electric-dipole–allowed orientational mechanism for chiral-specific fluorescence in uniaxial systems. These observations elevate fluorescence as a novel chiral-specific probe with exquisite sensitivity to chirality and interface specificity akin to that normally reserved for even-ordered nonlinear optical interactions, such as second harmonic and sum-frequency spectroscopy.

articles_hidden.title: Deep learning reveals ecological decoupling and rate heterogeneity in Hymenoptera wing evolution
articles_hidden.authors: Ancheng Peng, Shihan Guan, Laurent Albera, Régine Le Bouquin Jeannès, Huazhong Shu, Mathieu Boderau, André Nel, Bo Wang, Corentin Jouault, Frédéric Legendre
articles_hidden.abstract: Quantifying biomorphological evolution and integrating phenotypic data into large-scale ecological and evolutionary studies are often limited by the scalability, subjectivity, and poor interpretability of existing methods. We introduce HAIKA (Hierarchical Attention-based Interpretable K-dimensional Autoencoder), a self-supervised residual channel-attention autoencoder that extracts continuous morphological representations from unlabeled standardized images and highlights the image regions that contribute to those representations. Applied to insect forewings across broad pterygote lineages, HAIKA outperformed most baseline deep learning models and conventional descriptors in clustering, dimensionality reduction, and morphological embedding. When applied to Hymenoptera (i.e., ants, bees, and wasps), the HAIKA-derived continuous characters improved morphology-based phylogenetic reconstruction and illuminated the evolutionary dynamics of wing shape and venation. Our results reveal that wing morphological evolution in Hymenoptera proceeds at decoupled rates across shape and venation modules and is not consistently aligned with key ecological transitions such as parasitoidism or eusociality. HAIKA provides a scalable, image-based route for phenotypic analyses, broadly applicable across diverse taxa and to both 2D and 3D datasets.

articles_hidden.title: A bifunctional actuator to correct loss-of-function deficits in cardiac voltage-gated sodium channels
articles_hidden.authors: Lucile Fossier, Marc Yehya, Richard Z. Zhuang, Sri Karthika Shanmugam, Ryan Mahling, Timothy Cho, Audrey Kochiss, Allen L. Hsu, Sandra B. Gabelli, Gordana Vunjak-Novakovic, Henry M. Colecraft, Manu Ben-Johny
articles_hidden.abstract: Despite their emerging prominence, ion channelopathies have remained challenging to correct, as ion channel dysfunction linked to disease is multifaceted, involving changes in activity and/or localization. Yet, current corrective strategies typically focus on restoring only one aspect leading to incomplete efficacy. Here, focusing on the voltage-gated sodium channel, Na V 1.5, whose dysfunction is linked to life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias, we develop a genetically encoded bifunctional actuator as a proof-of-concept molecular strategy to reverse pathophysiological changes in channel function. Specifically, we engineer a high affinity nanobody targeting Na V 1.5 with two moieties: (i) a peptide that restores proper inactivation and (ii) a linkage-specific deubiquitinase that promotes surface-membrane localization. Functional validation in heterologous systems and in human and mouse cardiomyocytes demonstrated restoration of Na V 1.5 trafficking and/or gating. In all, this approach shows promise for reversing molecular deficits observed with Na V channelopathies and provides a framework to engineer multifunctional modulators targeting ion channelopathies.

articles_hidden.title: Senescent tumor cell membrane–based “time engine” nanosystem amplifies endoplasmic reticulum targeting for metastasis blockade
articles_hidden.authors: Jing Tao, Yuzhen Guo, Fengzhi Zhang, Jiahui Wu, Liyun Xing, Jinxia Kong, Lian Li, Zhou Zhou, Yuan Huang
articles_hidden.abstract: As an important component of biomimetic drug delivery systems, cell membrane–coated nanoparticles are widely used for subcellular delivery. However, the influence of cell membranes at different life cycles on subcellular delivery remains unexplored. Our previous study demonstrated that senescent tumor cell membrane–coated nanoparticles (SNP) displayed superior endoplasmic reticulum (ER) targeting efficiency in tumor cells. After inducing tumor cells into senescence, SNP showed greater accumulation in ER. Herein, we design a “time engine” nanosystem for amplified ER targeting: Firstly, ribociclib is encapsulated into SNP (R@SNP) to induce tumor cell senescence; then, SNP loaded with brefeldin A (B@SNP) is used to trigger ER stress. By sequential therapy, R@SNP disrupts the cytoskeleton of 4T1 tumor cells to eliminate ER-targeting barriers and remodels the tumor immune microenvironment; B@SNP boosts ER-targeting efficiency and triggers intense ER stress. Collectively, such time engine nanosystem achieves excellent ER accumulation and antimetastatic efficacy in 4T1 tumor–bearing mice, providing an innovative perspective for subcellular delivery and tumor treatment.

articles_hidden.title: Enhancer binding kinetics explain transcription factor hub formation
articles_hidden.authors: Samantha Fallacaro, Manya Kapoor, Lillian Encarnation, Apratim Mukherjee, Meghan A. Turner, Hernan G. Garcia, Mustafa Mir
articles_hidden.abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) form dynamic, high-concentration clusters, condensates, or hubs, proposed to increase TF binding frequency at target enhancers. However, how enhancer sequence shapes hub properties remains unclear. We developed a live imaging–based framework to quantify the spatiotemporal relationship between TF hubs and actively transcribed genes in live Drosophila embryos. Examining hubs formed by the TF Dorsal across enhancers with defined binding site composition, we find that hub enrichment and persistence scale with the number of Dorsal binding motifs. However, these hub properties do not predict transcriptional bursts for a given enhancer. Combining quantitative imaging with computational modeling, we show that Dorsal hub formation can be explained by TF-DNA binding kinetics alone. These findings support a model in which TF hubs emerge from enhancer-encoded TF-DNA interactions rather than higher-order regulatory assemblies.

articles_hidden.title: Remote allosteric control of single-atom Cu sites in Zr-MOFs enables selective CH 4 hydroxylation
articles_hidden.authors: Geqian Fang, Fenfei Wei, Wenjun Yu, Yu Kang, Maya Marinova, Lulu Chen, Lin Li, Vitaly V. Ordomsky, Anne-Marie Blanchenet, Sen Lin, Jian Lin, Xiaodong Wang, Xianzhi Fu, Andrei Y. Khodakov, Tao Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Highly selective oxidation of methane to liquid oxygenates under mild conditions remains challenging because of the difficulty in controlling overoxidation at highly reactive sites. Here, we demonstrate remote control of single-atom Cu reactivity through outer-shell coordination engineering in Zr-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). By anchoring Cu 1 to Zr-oxo nodes in UiO-66-X (X = -NO 2 , -H, and -CH 3 ), remote X-BDC ligands systematically modulate the electronic properties of Cu 1 sites and the catalytic microenvironment. In situ characterization combined with ab initio molecular dynamics in an explicitly solvated aqueous environment reveals a dynamic outer-shell-to-inner-shell regulation that reshapes the active structure and reactive oxygen species around Cu 1 sites, thereby facilitating CH 4 activation. In particular, the electron-withdrawing NO 2 -BDC ligand creates electron-deficient Cu 1 - • OH* sites, while adsorbed water further regulates active-site conformation. Consequently, Cu 1 /U6-NO 2 achieves a turnover frequency of 322.4 h −1 with nearly 100% oxygenate selectivity under mild conditions, establishing a general strategy for overcoming activity-selectivity trade-offs in methane conversion.

articles_hidden.title: Carbonic anhydrase VIII regulates IP3R1-dependent Ca 2+ signaling to coordinate insulin secretion and hepatic glucose production
articles_hidden.authors: Muhammad Fauzi, Takaaki Murakami, Ryota Usui, Ainur Botagarova, Daisuke Otani, Kentarou Sakaki, Shinsuke Tokumoto, Toshinori Imaizumi, Hisato Tatsuoka, Masahito Ogura, Jonathan Campbell, Nobuya Inagaki, Daisuke Yabe
articles_hidden.abstract: Intracellular Ca 2+ signaling is essential for glucose-induced insulin secretion (GIIS) and hepatic glucose production (HGP), yet how Ca 2+ dynamics are coordinated across organs remains unclear. Carbonic anhydrase VIII (CA8), an endogenous inhibitor of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor 1 (IP3R1), was identified as a shared regulator of pancreatic and hepatic glucose metabolism. Using Car8 wdl mice, we showed that CA8 deficiency enhanced GIIS and HGP in vivo and ex vivo. In islets and hepatocytes, CA8 loss augments Ca 2+ oscillations, an effect abolished by IP3R inhibition or Car8 reexpression. Enhanced HGP persists independently of glucagon receptor, PLC, or PKA signaling and occurs without increased IP 1 , indicating heightened IP3R1 sensitivity rather than increased IP 3 production. In hepatocytes, chronic glucagon exposure attenuated acute glucagon responsiveness in a CA8-dependent manner. In obese diabetic mice, CA8 increased in islets but decreased in hepatocytes; hepatic CA8 restoration reduced excessive HGP. Collectively, these findings identify CA8 as a cross-organ regulator of IP3R1-dependent Ca 2+ signaling with translational relevance to diabetes.

articles_hidden.title: TIME FOR COFFEE coordinates phase separation and chromatin regulation for salt tolerance
articles_hidden.authors: Wenwen Tian, Xinheng Lyu, Grace R. Qian, Xuehua Zhong
articles_hidden.abstract: The circadian clock enhances plant fitness by aligning internal timing with the external photoperiod, but how it coordinates spatiotemporal regulation with chromatin dynamics to improve salt tolerance is not well understood. Here, we show that the clock component TIME FOR COFFEE (TIC) forms biomolecular condensates in response to salt stress, but not to osmotic stress alone. Consistently, tic mutants were hypersensitive to salt stress yet displayed enhanced salt tolerance under 21-hour light-dark cycles matching their shortened circadian period, highlighting the importance of circadian clock in salt tolerance. Salt stress increases H3K9ac levels at the salt stress–responsive genes and induces their expression in a time-of-day–dependent manner in wild-type plants, whereas both H3K9ac level and transcriptional activation are attenuated in tic mutants. TIC physically associates with HD2-type histone deacetylases, and a subset of HD2 partially colocalizes with TIC condensates in the nucleolus under salt stress. Genetic and biochemical analyses showed that salt stress promotes TIC condensate formation, accompanied by reduced HD2 occupancy at salt stress–responsive loci, thereby elevating H3K9ac levels and promoting gene expression. Together, these findings uncover a mechanism by which salt-induced TIC condensate formation links chromatin regulation with circadian timing, thereby promoting plant adaptation to salt stress.

articles_hidden.title: Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses
articles_hidden.authors: Yona Tugg, Jann C. Ang, Imran Ahmed, Rikin Mehta, Viraj Mane, Sam Afkhami, Matthew S. Miller
articles_hidden.abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk–derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.

articles_hidden.title: On-fault and remote observations of exceptionally long, supershear rupture in the 2025 M 7.7 Mandalay earthquake
articles_hidden.authors: Kejie Chen, Haoran Meng, Zhenguo Zhang, Zijia Wang, Zaiwang Liu, Chris Milliner, Guoguang Wei, Fuhua Zheng, Jianhao Gao, Min Zhou, Solene L. Antoine, Chaofeng Wang, Zhongqiu He, Kai Huang, Jindong Song, Qiang Ma, Haipeng Luo, Xiaofei Chen, Jean-Philippe Avouac
articles_hidden.abstract: Straight faults are considered prone to large supershear ruptures and seismic gaps to likely host future earthquakes. Both predictions may have been fulfilled in the magnitude ( M ) 7.7 Mandalay earthquake of 28 March 2025 on the Sagaing Fault. Exceptional video footage of the fault rupture, high-rate Global Navigation Satellite System, and seismological and remote sensing data reveal a supershear slip pulse that formed early and ruptured a well-identified seismic gap but propagated well beyond it, resulting in an exceptional rupture length of 510 kilometers. By contrast, the slip pulse observed in the video footage has subshear characteristics. These observations can be reconciled by a preferred conceptual interpretation invoking depth-dependent weakening properties, stress heterogeneity, and possible dynamic triggering. These properties allow for energetic ruptures that stay confined to the depth range locked in the interseismic period but are not confined to seismic gaps along strike.

articles_hidden.title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment
articles_hidden.authors: Yin Li, Qin Ran, Anying Xiong, Manling Jiang, Fengkai Xu, Yongqi Wei, Jie Gu, Guoping Li, Di Ge, Chunlai Lu
articles_hidden.abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). Clinically, UPP1 expression in TAMs and TANs correlates with poor prognosis and diminished response to immunotherapy across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, UPP1 up-regulation could be driven by NF-κB signaling. Functionally, UPP1 reprograms macrophages toward a tumor-promoting phenotype, characterized by enhanced glycolysis, ATP-adenosine signaling activation, and increased production of immunosuppressive cytokines such as granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. In neutrophils, UPP1 also supports TAN polarization, influences neutrophil extracellular trap release, and contributes to broad immunosuppressive remodeling. In vivo, targeting UPP1 in macrophages or neutrophils reprograms the immune landscape and restrains tumor progression. Together, our findings uncover a previously underappreciated role of UPP1 in nonmalignant immune populations and establish it as a key immune mediator within the TME, offering a potentially promising therapeutic target for enhancing antitumor immunity.

articles_hidden.title: Scalable design of fluidic DEMUX/MUX
articles_hidden.authors: Hwayeong Jeong, Jamie Paik, Jung Kim
articles_hidden.abstract: Fluidic logic circuits offer a foundation for decentralized onboard control in soft pneumatic robots, enabling their integration into actuator networks to generate complex movements. However, existing fluidic controllers in soft robots face scalability limitations, restricting their ability to handle growing degrees of freedom across sizes while preserving compliance. Here, we present a scalable fluidic control architecture that integrates high-radix demultiplexing with time multiplexing to achieve a high input-to-output ratio and reprogrammable actuation. We incorporate a design method based on dimensionless parameters to preserve comparable valve opening and closing pressure thresholds across different physical scales, thereby maintaining consistent addressing behavior of the demultiplexer after geometric scaling. In addition, structural stretchability enables seamless integration into soft bodies, maintaining reliable control under dynamic deformation without compromising compliance. This hybrid demultiplexer/multiplexer fluidic circuit overcomes key limitations, offering functional scalability, geometric scalability, and physical integrability in a single architecture. Our approach enables autonomous, adaptable soft robots capable of complex, multifunctional motions, functioning as self-contained systems.

articles_hidden.title: SMCHD1 is a target for gene activation therapy to treat Prader-Willi syndrome
articles_hidden.authors: Megan Iminitoff, Anna Le Fevre, Tamara Cameron, Hannah K. Vanyai, Caleb Chew, Sarah A. Kinkel, Kelsey Breslin, Susanne Theiß, Quentin Gouil, Merlin Thomas, James M. Murphy, Christian P. Schaaf, Andrew Keniry, Marnie E. Blewitt
articles_hidden.abstract: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss of expression from the active paternal allele at an imprinted cluster on chromosome 15. Current treatments address individual symptoms rather than the underlying cause of disease. Because all patients preserve a normal but epigenetically silenced maternal copy of these genes, activation of this copy offers a potential disease-modifying therapy. Here, we investigated the epigenetic regulator SMCHD1. First, we demonstrated that SMCHD1 represses the PWS locus in both mice and humans, supporting its relevance as a therapeutic target. Second, we found that SMCHD1 represses the entire PWS locus in neural lineages, extending its previously known role beyond only part of the cluster. Deleting Smchd1 after early development in vivo activated PWS genes in disease-relevant mouse tissues including hypothalamus and improved phenotypes in a PWS mouse model. Despite broader genome-wide binding, postearly development targeting of SMCHD1 appeared remarkably safe, supporting its potential for gene activation therapy for PWS.

articles_hidden.title: An inspiration-off attractor supports the robust and flexible control of breathing
articles_hidden.authors: Nicholas E. Bush, Luiz M. Oliveira, Zachary T. Glovak, Jan-Marino Ramirez
articles_hidden.abstract: Breathing is a fundamental motor rhythm necessary to sustain life. The rhythm and pattern of breathing arises from the coordination of a rostrocaudally extended ventral respiratory column (VRC) in the medulla. Although recurrent excitation is sufficient for rhythmic bursting in reduced in vitro preparations, comparatively less is understood about how inhibition and excitation interact with feedback circuits to generate the breathing rhythm in vivo. Here, we expand on the classical “inspiratory-off switch” model that inhibitory signaling from lung stretch afferent pathways plays a critical role in generating the breathing rhythm in vivo. We perform high-density extracellular recordings along the length of the VRC during optogenetic and physiological manipulations and apply computational analyses to characterize how these perturbations govern low-dimensional neural dynamics. We show that stimulation of GABAergic afferents of the nucleus of the solitary tract advance or delay breathing in a manner similar to, but quantitatively distinct from, inhibition local to the VRC. We use generative dynamical models to show that inhibitory activity controls respiratory activity through transient stabilization of an attractive region of the low-dimensional manifold corresponding to expiration. Together, these results propose an “inspiratory-off attractor” model that underlies network level control of breathing in vivo.

articles_hidden.title: Comprehensive characterization of transposable element expression reveals regulatory circuitry and clinical implications in cancers
articles_hidden.authors: Wei Hu, Wenjun Jiang, Zehua Gao, Teng Liu, Yuzhu Fang, Chenyang Zhang, Yunzhe Wang, Xiwen Yang, Xinyi Zhang, Liya Su, Katie W. Gu, Qianfeng Wang, Bo Wen, Zhao Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) constitute nearly half of the human genome and have crucial roles in regulatory networks and clinical utility in cancers.
